The question is about whether all ethnic groups in New Zealand show similar socio-economic health disparities. While many ethnic groups generally experience similar socio-economic health risks, some groups (such as Pacific and Asian communities) tend to have less pronounced or deeper socio-economic health gradients compared to others. This suggests that caution should be exercised when using deprivation or other socio-economic measures as proxy indicators for the need of healthcare services in these populations.

To summarize:

- Many ethnic groups generally experience similar socio-economic health risks.
- However, some groups (such as Pacific and Asian communities) tend to have less pronounced or deeper socio-economic health gradients compared to others.
